assessment.nobel_worthiness: The three-step picture gave a simple, powerful physical account of electron recollision and underlies high-harmonic and attosecond science.
assessment.attribution: The credited theorists represent central complementary formulations of the recollision framework, though the broader experimental and theoretical field is substantial.
assessment.maturity: Its predictions have been repeatedly tested across strong-field experiments and have enabled an extensive mature research field.
uncertainties: The appropriate boundary between this theoretical foundation and already recognized attosecond experimental advances needs careful consideration.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks are a profound advance in controlling atoms and measuring time, with exceptional precision and broad fundamental reach.
assessment.attribution: Katori and Ye are highly visible pioneers of the lattice-clock concept and its decisive realization.
assessment.maturity: Independent clocks now operate at the stated precision and support demanding comparisons and fundamental tests.
uncertainties: Credit across the wider frequency-metrology community requires close historical review.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Atom interferometry transformed coherent atomic motion into a sensitive probe of gravity, inertial effects, and quantum physics.
assessment.attribution: The three names capture foundational theory, landmark interferometric demonstrations, and precision-measurement development.
assessment.maturity: The methods have been replicated widely and have delivered both fundamental tests and durable precision-sensing capabilities.
uncertainties: The scope is broad, and selecting three people from its many essential contributors is difficult.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Controlled trapping and precision spectroscopy of antimatter offer unusually direct tests of matter-antimatter symmetry.
assessment.attribution: Gabrielse and Hangst have led distinct, central experimental programs that made precision antimatter measurements possible.
assessment.maturity: Antihydrogen production, trapping, and spectroscopy have advanced from feasibility demonstrations to reproducible precision experiments.
uncertainties: The ultimate sensitivity of symmetry tests and the most appropriate allocation of credit remain evolving.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Titanium-sapphire technology and passive mode locking made robust femtosecond lasers broadly available and reshaped ultrafast science.
assessment.attribution: The proposed names correspond to the laser medium and two influential routes to compact passive mode locking.
assessment.maturity: The techniques have been used for decades throughout ultrafast optics, including the later development of attosecond science.
uncertainties: The interwoven technical history of femtosecond-laser development makes attribution unusually complex.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Geometric phase and the Aharonov-Bohm effect exposed nonclassical global features of quantum mechanics with lasting conceptual and experimental consequences.
assessment.attribution: Berry and Aharonov are inseparably associated with the two named foundational phenomena.
assessment.maturity: Both effects have extensive experimental support and have become standard elements of quantum physics.
uncertainties: The historical conceptual lineage and the relation between the two effects merit careful credit analysis.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattices have made strongly correlated quantum many-body models experimentally accessible with exceptional control.
assessment.attribution: These experimental leaders made defining demonstrations and established a versatile platform; theoretical credit is also substantial.
assessment.maturity: The platform is widely reproduced and has generated a mature body of precision many-body experiments.
uncertainties: The field has more major contributors than the prize limit can accommodate.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Circuit QED established a remarkably controllable solid-state realization of strong light-matter coupling and quantum measurement.
assessment.attribution: Blais, Schoelkopf, and Girvin represent key theoretical and experimental contributions to the field's formative architecture.
assessment.maturity: The phenomena are robustly reproduced and now form a central experimental quantum platform.
uncertainties: Rapid continuing progress makes it harder to separate the original conceptual achievement from later engineering development.
